newsitem.title: USA: Brent crude trades up in U.S. aftermarket.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude trades up in U.S. aftermarket.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude traded up in the U.S. aftermarket on Tuesday, with a Wall Street house again playing a starring role, traders said.
Two full boats of September Brent switched hands at $18.70 and $18.71 a barrel, compared to the IPE close of $18.59 a barrel.
Partial cargoes traded from $18.64 to $18.69 a barrel.
August/September Brent was thin, with one deal heard done at 16.5 cents a barrel. The spread was widely pegged at plus 13 to 18 cents.
September/October moved at minus four cents, with the spread assessed at minus four to minus three cents.
October/November was pegged at minus 10 to minus seven cents.
